message.content:
You have web access: load tools via ToolSearch query "select:WebFetch,WebSearch" and use them; you may also use curl via the Bash tool (add a realistic browser User-Agent header, e.g. Chrome on Windows). Verify claims with REAL requests where possible — do not answer purely from memory. Report only what you actually observed or found in current sources.

Investigate how to programmatically obtain GAME DETAIL and REVIEW data from Metacritic's current (2025/2026) website. Pick 1-2 recent games (find any recent title on https://www.metacritic.com/game/ or use a known one like a 2025 release) and verify on their pages:

1. Game detail page https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/ — how to extract: title, cover image URL, description, developer, publisher, genres, release date, trailer/video URL, and the list of platforms where EACH platform has its own Metascore and Userscore. Check whether the data sits in embedded JSON (__NEXT_DATA__ or similar) or needs an API call. Note: does the page show per-platform scores directly, or does each platform have its own page variant (e.g. ?platform= or /game/{platform}/{slug})?
2. Critic reviews: https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/critic-reviews/ — how to get review text snippets, reviewer name, score; pagination.
3. User reviews: https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/user-reviews/ — same questions.
4. Look for underlying JSON API endpoints for reviews (e.g. backend.metacritic.com/reviews/... — WebSearch for open-source Metacritic scrapers on GitHub from 2023-2026 to find known endpoint patterns and apiKeys) and VERIFY with real requests.

Report concrete working endpoints/paths and field locations, plus observed anti-bot behavior and a recommended approach (primary + fallback).

attachment.content:
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
CF-Ray: a2e324bb1ca6970c-AMS
CF-Cache-Status: MISS
Server: cloudflare
Via: 1.1 google

findings: Metacritic's current site (verified 2026-08-20) is a Nuxt 3 SSR app; all data is served by a public JSON backend at https://backend.metacritic.com. Plain curl with a Chrome User-Agent gets HTTP 200 on both www pages and backend JSON; requests even work with NO User-Agent and NO apiKey (verified with real requests returning full data). Backend is behind Cloudflare (Server: cloudflare, CF-Ray header) but no challenge/block was triggered during ~20 requests.

A publishable apiKey is embedded in every page's HTML: apiKey=1MOZgmNFxvmljaQR1X9KAij9Mo4xAY3u (found 73 backend.metacritic.com references in the game page source; the key appears in dropdown/footers component URLs). It is currently optional for the games/reviews endpoints but should be sent anyway and re-scraped from page HTML if it rotates.

GAME DETAIL (verified for clair-obscur-expedition-33 and death-stranding-2-on-the-beach): GET https://backend.metacritic.com/games/metacritic/{slug}/web?apiKey=...&componentName=product returns data.item with: title, slug, description, releaseDate (2025-04-24), rating (ESRB 'M'), premiereYear, genres[] ({id,name}), production.companies[] (typeName 'Developer'=Sandfall Interactive / 'Publisher'=Kepler Interactive), production.crew[] (director/writers/cast), images[] (typeName 'mainImage'/'cardImage' with bucketPath), video (title, duration, jwPlayerId, manifestUrl=https://cdn.jwplayer.com/manifests/{jwPlayerId}.m3u8, embedUrl=https://cdn.jwplayer.com/players/{jwPlayerId}.html), criticScoreSummary (lead-platform Metascore, reviewCount, positive/neutral/negative counts, sentiment), and platforms[].

PER-PLATFORM SCORES: there is ONE canonical game page per title (no /game/{platform}/{slug} variants); platform variants are query params on review pages (?platform=pc). In the product JSON, data.item.platforms[] gives each platform's own {name, slug, isLeadPlatform, releaseDate, relatedGameId, criticScoreSummary{score, reviewCount, positive/neutral/negative, sentiment}} — verified PS5=92, PC=91, Xbox Series X=91. Platforms[] does NOT include user scores; the top-level criticScoreSummary is the lead platform's score.

PER-PLATFORM USERSCORE: GET https://backend.metacritic.com/reviews/metacritic/user/games/{slug}/platform/{platform-slug}/stats/web?apiKey=... returns data.item {max:10, score, reviewCount, positiveCount, neutralCount, negativeCount, sentiment} — verified PC=9.6 (6109 reviews), PS5=9.5 (26806), XSX=9.6 (1805). Omitting /platform/{x}/ returns the LEAD platform's stats, not an all-platform aggregate. Same pattern with 'critic' instead of 'user' gives per-platform Metascore stats. Note: a query param ?filterByPlatform=pc is silently IGNORED — the platform must be a PATH segment.

CRITIC REVIEWS: GET https://backend.metacritic.com/reviews/metacritic/critic/games/{slug}/web?apiKey=...&offset=0&limit=N (all platforms mixed; add /platform/{platform-slug}/ before /web for one platform — verified PC subset totalResults=60 vs 86 overall). Each item: quote (review snippet), score (0-100), url (external full review), date, author, authorSlug, publicationName, publicationSlug, platform, reviewedProduct{platform{id,name}}. Response data.totalResults + HATEOAS links.next/prev/first/last for pagination; supports &sort=score|date|publication and &filterBySentiment=all|positive|neutral|negative.

USER REVIEWS: GET https://backend.metacritic.com/reviews/metacritic/user/games/{slug}/web?apiKey=...&offset=0&limit=N — same envelope/pagination. Each item: id (uuid), quote (full review text), score (0-10 integer), date, author (username), spoiler (bool), thumbsUp/thumbsDown, platform, reviewedProduct. Verified totalResults=6697 for Clair Obscur; limit=100 and even limit=500 both returned that many items in one call (no strict small cap observed); offset paginates.

IMAGE URLS: images[].bucketPath (e.g. /provider/7/2/7-1743138161.jpg) maps to https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/catalog{bucketPath} — verified 200 image/jpeg (620KB original). The site's resized/webp variant format is https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/{hash}/catalog{bucketPath}?auto=webp&fit=crop&height=H&width=W (hash values appear in ld+json/page HTML; the un-resized /a/img/catalog form needs no hash).

HTML FALLBACK: the game detail page embeds a schema.org VideoGame ld+json block (name, description, datePublished, contentRating, genre, gamePlatform[], publisher[], image, screenshots, aggregateRating = overall Metascore+reviewCount, trailer with jwplayer m3u8 contentUrl) — easy to parse but lacks developer, userscore, and per-platform scores. The Nuxt payload is __NUXT_DATA__ (Nuxt 3 array/ref hydration format, awkward to parse). Review list pages (critic-reviews/, user-reviews/) contain NO SSR review content — reviews load client-side from the backend API, so HTML scraping of review pages requires JS rendering; the API is the only practical path.

DISCOVERY: GET https://backend.metacritic.com/finder/metacritic/web?apiKey=...&sortBy=-releaseDate&productType=games&offset=0&limit=N returns a browsable catalog (verified totalResults=35435; items include title, slug, releaseDate, criticScoreSummary) — usable to enumerate game slugs; also supports sortBy=-metaScore and -popularityCount. Additional verified endpoints: .../reviews/metacritic/{critic|user}/games/{slug}/summary/web (score summary component), https://backend.metacritic.com/games/metacritic/{familyId}/stats/web (player ratings/playtime/difficulty poll data; familyId = gameTaxonomy.family.id e.g. 1200631965), and .../games/metacritic/{slug}/wheretobuy/web.

GitHub prior art: davutbayik/metacritic-backend-scraper (Python, uses these same backend.metacritic.com endpoints for games/movies/TV) confirms the endpoint family is stable and publicly used; older scrapers (marcalencc, Markel/metacritic-crawler etc.) target the pre-2023 HTML site and are obsolete. Sources: https://github.com/davutbayik/metacritic-backend-scraper, https://github.com/marcalencc/metacritic-scraper, https://github.com/Markel/metacritic-crawler.
endpoints: https://backend.metacritic.com/games/metacritic/{slug}/web?apiKey=1MOZgmNFxvmljaQR1X9KAij9Mo4xAY3u — game detail JSON (title, description, developer/publisher in production.companies, genres, images, video, per-platform Metascores in data.item.platforms[]). Send a browser User-Agent header; apiKey currently optional.

https://backend.metacritic.com/reviews/metacritic/critic/games/{slug}/web?apiKey=...&offset=0&limit=50[&sort=score|date|publication][&filterBySentiment=all|positive|neutral|negative] — critic reviews; paginate via offset/limit or links.next; data.totalResults gives count.

https://backend.metacritic.com/reviews/metacritic/critic/games/{slug}/platform/{platform-slug}/web?apiKey=...&offset=0&limit=50 — critic reviews for one platform (platform-slug e.g. pc, playstation-5, xbox-series-x; from platforms[].slug).

https://backend.metacritic.com/reviews/metacritic/user/games/{slug}/web?apiKey=...&offset=0&limit=100 — user reviews (score 0-10, full text in quote, author, date, spoiler); same /platform/{platform-slug}/ variant and pagination; limit up to at least 500 worked.

https://backend.metacritic.com/reviews/metacritic/user/games/{slug}/platform/{platform-slug}/stats/web?apiKey=... — per-platform Userscore {score, reviewCount, sentiment, positive/neutral/negative}; swap 'user'->'critic' for per-platform Metascore stats; without /platform/ segment it returns the LEAD platform only.
https://backend.metacritic.com/games/metacritic/{familyId}/stats/web?apiKey=... — player poll stats (ratings histogram, playtime, difficulty); familyId from product JSON gameTaxonomy.family.id.
https://cdn.jwplayer.com/manifests/{jwPlayerId}.m3u8 — trailer video stream from data.item.video.jwPlayerId (manifestUrl field gives it directly).
https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/ — HTML page; contains ld+json VideoGame block and the current apiKey in source (fallback / key refresh).
input.recommendation: Primary: skip HTML scraping entirely and call the backend JSON API directly. Per game: (1) GET backend.metacritic.com/games/metacritic/{slug}/web for title/description/developer/publisher/genres/release date/rating/images/trailer plus platforms[] with per-platform Metascores; (2) for each platforms[].slug, GET reviews/metacritic/user/games/{slug}/platform/{p}/stats/web for the per-platform Userscore; (3) page through reviews/metacritic/{critic|user}/games/{slug}/web (or the /platform/{p}/web variant) with offset/limit (limit=100 is safe, follow links.next until offset >= data.totalResults). Always send a realistic Chrome User-Agent, include the apiKey (1MOZgmNFxvmljaQR1X9KAij9Mo4xAY3u, re-extract from any page's HTML with regex apiKey=([A-Za-z0-9]+) if it stops working), throttle to ~1 req/sec, and build image URLs as www.metacritic.com/a/img/catalog{bucketPath}. Fallback: fetch the game page HTML with curl+browser UA and parse the schema.org ld+json block (gives title, description, publisher, genre, platforms list, overall Metascore, images, trailer m3u8) — but this lacks developer, userscores, per-platform scores, and reviews; for reviews there is no HTML fallback without JS rendering (review pages hydrate client-side), so a headless browser (Playwright intercepting the backend XHRs) is the last-resort fallback if Cloudflare starts challenging plain HTTP clients.
risks: The apiKey and the backend URL structure are unofficial and undocumented; Fandom can rotate the key or change paths at any time — always re-derive the key from page HTML rather than hardcoding only.

Backend is behind Cloudflare (CF-Ray observed): no challenge at low request rates today, but aggressive crawling (large offsets, high parallelism) may trigger 403/429 or JS challenges; keep ~1 req/sec and realistic headers.

The 'overall' stats/score endpoints without a /platform/ segment silently return the LEAD platform, and ?filterByPlatform= is silently ignored — easy to record wrong per-platform numbers if you use query params instead of the /platform/{slug}/ path segment.

User review totals are large (6,697 text reviews / 26,806 ratings for one game) — full pagination is many requests; quote field for critic reviews is only a snippet (full review lives on the external publication URL).
Scraping may conflict with Metacritic/Fandom Terms of Use; data (esp. review text) is copyrighted — fine for personal/research use, risky to republish at scale.
images[].bucketPath sometimes needs the bucketType prefix (observed 'catalog'); other bucketTypes may map to different /a/img/ roots — handle unknown types defensively.
Slug discovery via the finder endpoint returns 35k+ games including unscored shovelware; filter by criticScoreSummary.score != null if you need scored titles only.
